findings.title: An unreadable workspace-settings.json is treated as empty, then overwritten on the next update
findings.body: `MachineSettingsStore.open` catches every `readFile` error and returns an empty store (lines 218-222). It does not tell ENOENT apart from EACCES/EIO/EBUSY. The next `update()` (lines 244-261) calls `write()`, which serializes the whole in-memory map (lines 268-270) and atomically replaces the file. So one transient read failure at launch, followed by any override edit or Use/Ignore answer, permanently deletes every other workspace's machine-bound `uploadMode` and every accepted folder-file record. This happens with no error or log. Losing `uploadMode` matters: a workspace the user set to `local-only` silently falls back to the All level (for example `automatic`), so files start uploading without consent. Losing the records puts every confirmed folder file back to `pending`. The corrupt-JSON path has a similar gap: if the `rename` aside fails (line 265), that is swallowed and the write goes ahead over the file. Suggested fix: return an empty store only for ENOENT. For any other code, mark the store unusable, so writes refuse or retry, or so it re-reads before the first write. Don't overwrite the file in that state.

findings.title: refresh(target) inside persistActive broadcasts before commit, and a throw there leaves the registry switched but the switch reported failed
findings.body: `reg.setActive(target)` runs first, so `activeId()` is already the target. `WorkspaceSettings.refresh` (workspace-settings.ts:96-98) therefore calls `changed()` → `notifyOverridesChanged()`. That runs every main settings listener and broadcasts `settings:changed` with the target's effective settings while the gate is still closed and windows are still stamped to the old workspace (switch-transaction.ts:70-80). The `notifyOverridesChanged()` in `afterCommit` then does nothing, so the comment 'ready the moment it commits' doesn't hold. Separately, if anything in that refresh throws (`reg.availability` in `isAvailable`, or a settings listener inside `changed()`), `persistActive` rejects after the registry has already persisted the target. switch-transaction.ts:73-76 then reopens the gate on the old workspace and reports failure, while `reg.active()` names the new one. Could the refresh run without notifying (or be caught) inside `persistActive`, with the notification left to `afterCommit` alone?
